scoreboard.gtm_channel: ProductHunt + IndieHackers launch with $29/$99 Stripe checkout live
Twitter/X viral clip — paste-URL hero with 10-min countdown
Slack App Directory + 5 design-partner VC workspaces
Leaderboard screenshots auto-shareable to X — earned virality flywheel
HN Show HN with curl one-liner — terminal-native crowd

rationale: P21 is the only card that resolves monetization_model='unknown' into a defensible price ladder ($29 Hacker / $99 Founder) that the 1M-context Opus 4.7 capability can actually underwrite via per-preview unit economics. It preserves every downstream pricing surface (free tier as satirical lead-gen, $29 conversion floor, $99 Founder ceiling, future enterprise upsell to P17). The satire becomes a CAC engine, not a dead-end joke. Stripe Checkout + usage meter on Day 1 means hackathon judges see real billing logic — Arize-track 'serious agent engineers' signal, not a screenshot demo. Composite 50/60 with the highest pricing optionality score across all 26 cards.

honorable_mentions.P03: Highest virality + clearest GTM (single-CTA paste-URL). Best 3-min judging clip candidate. Loses on moat (1-day cloneable surface).
honorable_mentions.P08: Best B2B distribution into VC partner Slacks — secondary persona TAM is larger than primary indie hacker TAM at enterprise pricing.
honorable_mentions.P23: Leaderboard creates UGC flywheel; every spec-fit ≥95% screenshot is free marketing. Pricing optionality weakest of top 5.
honorable_mentions.P01: Strongest aggro-tone fit ('curl > React'). HN crown candidate. TAM ceiling is the bottleneck.

dissent_items: P21 risks looking mercenary in a satire product — pricing chrome could undercut the 'while they hire we ship' moral high ground.
P03 has no moat: any YC team clones the paste-URL hero in 4 hours. Story without defensibility = press cycle, not company.
P23 leaderboard requires real submissions to feel alive — chicken/egg problem for hackathon demo with no users yet.
P08 Slack Bot may fail hackathon's web-platform requirement on a strict reading; auxiliary web dashboard mitigates but is risk.
P01 CLI-first cuts off the VC secondary persona entirely — leaves 40-50% of TAM on the table.
P11 (Pragmatist) is too boring for a satire product — scored lowest on story strength; correct to exclude despite engineering virtue.
P17 Enterprise has the highest TAM/price but zero hackathon-day virality — wrong stage of company for this run.
P10 Dreamer's 200-company swarm is unfalsifiable in a 3-min demo — judges will smell vaporware.
P26 Anti-AI hides the Arize-track signal — strategically wrong for THIS hackathon track even if commercially defensible.
Top 5 is heavily indie-hacker-skewed; only P08 covers the VC secondary persona — meta-tally should weight that gap.

axis_observations.tam_ceiling: Indie-hacker SaaS at $29/$99 = realistic $50K-200K MRR ceiling year 1. Enterprise (P17) or VC-Slack (P08) unlock 5-10x but slower sales cycle.
axis_observations.pricing_traps: Free-forever framings (P04, P15, P20) feel honest but kill MRR. Cost-receipt ($0.043) is great marketing but bad as anchor.
axis_observations.moat_reality: The satire IS the moat. Phoenix self-improvement loop is technical moat. Brand voice (aggressive YC mockery) is hardest to clone — P01/P21/P23 best at internalizing it.
axis_observations.gtm_consensus: Single-CTA + paste-URL (P03) wins for hackathon demo; recurring-revenue (P21) wins for post-hackathon survival. Both must coexist.
axis_observations.channel_diversity: Top 5 covers: web (P03, P21), CLI/HN (P01), Slack (P08), gamified social (P23). Healthy spread.
